Use case · "best rated" shelf
Reach inside with dot notation
db.products.find({ "rating.rate": { $gte: 4.5 } })
rating
.
rate
Outer field, a dot, inner field — like a folder path.
Quotes are required around "rating.rate".
Result · 6 products
Silicon Power 256GB SSD · ★ 4.8 WD 4TB Gaming Drive · ★ 4.8 Mens Cotton Jacket · ★ 4.7 Womens Boat Neck Top · ★ 4.7 Naga Gold Bracelet · ★ 4.6 Womens Sports Tee · ★ 4.5

Order matters: sort first, then limit. -1 = high → low.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · "Price: low to high" dropdown = sort({ price: 1 })
Use case · the search bar
Titles that contain "jacket"
db.products.find({   title: { $regex: "jacket", $options: "i" } })
Result · 4 products
Mens Cotton Jacket Womens Snowboard Jacket Womens Faux Leather Jacket Womens Rain Jacket
$regex = "contains this pattern"
"i" = ignore case, so jacket finds Jacket
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · Try: "^Womens" (starts with) → 6 products
Use case · a price list · projection
Return only the fields you need
db.products.find({ category: "jewelery" }, { title: 1, price: 1, _id: 0 })
_id: 5, title: "Naga Gold Bracelet", price: 695, category: "jewelery", rating: { … }
title: "Naga Gold Bracelet", price: 695
1 = include
0 = hide
_id shows unless you hide it
Smaller documents = less data on the network → faster pages.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · Second argument of find() = projection
Use case · "Clothing" menu
Match any value in a list: $in
db.products.find({   category: { $in: ["men's clothing", "women's clothing"] } })
men's clothing · 4
women's clothing · 6
electronics
jewelery
10
products — one query instead of two
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · Opposite: $nin = "not in this list" → the other 10
Use case · combining filters
Both conditions, or either one
AND · just use a comma
db.products.find({   category: "electronics",   price: { $lt: 150 } })
4 results · WD 2TB, SanDisk SSD, Silicon Power SSD, WD 4TB
OR · use $or: [ … ]
db.products.find({ $or: [   { price: { $lt: 10 } },   { "rating.rate": { $gte: 4.7 } } ]})
6 results · 3 cheap items + 3 top-rated (Boat Neck Top is both — counted once)
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · Rule: AND narrows the list, OR widens it
Use case · "most reviewed" badge
One winner, one number
db.products.find()   .sort({ "rating.count": -1 })   .limit(1)
Womens Rain Jacket
679
reviews
db.products.countDocuments({   category: "electronics" })
Electronics in stock
6
products
MongoDB Series · Lecture 04 · countDocuments takes the same filter as find()
find() vs aggregate()
"How many per category?"
db.products.aggregate([   { $group: {     _id: "$category",     totalProducts: { $sum: 1 }   } } ])
find() picks documents. aggregate() computes new answers from them.
electronics
6
women's clothing
6
jewelery
4
men's clothing
4

Use case · pricing strategy
Average price per category
db.products.aggregate([   { $group: { _id: "$category", avgPrice: { $avg: "$price" } } } ])

Cheat sheet
"I want…" → what you write
Exact match
{ category: "jewelery" }
Any value in a list
{ category: { $in: [ … ] } }
Less / more than
{ price: { $lt: 50 } }
Either condition
{ $or: [ {…}, {…} ] }
A range
{ price: { $gte: 20, $lte: 100 } }
Only some fields
find(q, { title: 1, _id: 0 })
Inside a nested object
{ "rating.rate": { $gte: 4.5 } }
Top N
.sort({ price: -1 }).limit(5)
Text contains
{ title: { $regex: "x", $options: "i" } }
How many?
countDocuments(q)
